title: Choose CivicLens's new look
question: The layout stays. This picks the world it's drawn in: colour, type, density and one signature move, in both a light and a dark theme. Keep the roll, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Survey Plan
options.lineage: municipal survey and engineering drawings: plan sheets, title blocks, redline markup
options.thesis: Every issue is drawn like a surveyed plan: measured, dimensioned, and marked up in red when someone corrects it.
options.viewport: Same sidebar, map and panel; the map frame carries survey ticks, pins are survey markers with a dimensioned ±radius, and the panel opens as a sheet with a title block.
options.risk: Hairline drafting detail can turn fussy at phone size, and the dark theme must stay flat graphite, never glowing blueprint.

raised.raise: One measured module sets every panel, gap and row, and the map frame shows its ticks so the measure is visible.
Only content carries colour: category inks and evidence photos; every surface and control stays in the drawing's neutrals.
States are drawn marks, never glows: selected is filled, focus is bracketed, disabled is struck through.
A tight three-size type scale; rank comes from weight and small caps, not ever-bigger headings.
Selecting issues dims everything else on the map and in lists instead of adding highlight effects.

options.label: Locate Marks
options.lineage: the public-works utility-locate paint code sprayed on streets before a dig
options.thesis: The street crew's paint code becomes the interface: each issue type is a flat, matte locate colour marked on asphalt or concrete.
options.viewport: Same shell on an asphalt ground (concrete in light); pins become locate flags in the paint colours, the legend is the paint code, and the open issue gets a stencilled category band.
options.risk: Bright paint on dark asphalt is one step from the neon look you want to leave; it only works if every colour stays flat and matte.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: airport gate boards and segmented boarding passes
options.thesis: Issues as a live departure board: ranked by priority, and a changed issue moves in place and stays lit until someone has seen it.
options.viewport: Same shell; lists become a ranked board with fixed columns and one alert colour for changes, and the issue detail reads as a segmented pass.
options.case: Holds on recognition (everyone knows a departure board) but loses on clarity: it puts priority and change first, while this product's core truth is where an issue is and how sure we are.
options.risk: The map and the evidence can feel secondary to the ranking.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letters and layout built cell by cell on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: Grid hairlines over the whole shell, headline counts built from grid cells.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a type-design poster says nothing to residents or staff about streets and broken things.
options.kept: One measured module governs every panel, gap and row.
options.risk: Reads as a design exercise, not a civic tool.

options.label: Title Card Wall
options.thesis: Issue photos as rows of poster tiles that grow when focused.
options.viewport: Rows of evidence photos by category beside the map.
options.case: Fuses poorly: browsing issues like films trivialises triage, and many photos are withheld for privacy.
options.kept: Content carries the colour; the chrome stays neutral.
options.risk: Consumer-entertainment feel on a public-service tool.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.lineage: scholarly editions with keyed margin apparatus
options.thesis: Two dense columns round a rail of red keys, notes hung in wide margins.
options.viewport: Issue detail as an annotated page with keyed notes.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a reading layout fights a map-first working tool.
options.kept: States are drawn marks: filled, bracketed, struck.
options.risk: Bookish and slow for staff in a task.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: Everything at one type size on raked tinted slides over a lit goldenrod bed.
options.viewport: Panels raked at an angle across a lit bed.
options.case: Fuses poorly: slanted panels and a lit bed get in the way of a map and a table.
options.kept: Rank by weight and case, not size.
options.risk: Novelty over function on a working screen.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black and white barcode fields and sine lattices.
options.viewport: Issue density drawn as barcode columns.
options.case: Fuses poorly: abstract and strobing, unreadable for residents.
options.kept: Selection dims the field instead of highlighting.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The open-data portal look, done carefully: white cards, one blue accent, a clean map.
canonCard.viewport: Same shell in white and blue with card panels and standard pins.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every civic SaaS tool, which you said would feel wrong.
